Today, someone asked me whether an android app you install snoops over you?

To make an analogy, its akin to asking does your own appointed Doctor, Lawyer or Chartered Accountant snoop on you? If they want to snoop, of course they can do so because you have granted them access or privileges to certain aspects of your life. However, you usually trust them to not snoop over and misuse the information they have access to (otherwise, you wonâ€™t hire them in the first place, would you?)

Similarly, when you install an app from the Google Play Store, you grant the app certain privileges such as access to your Contacts, Call Logs, Camera, Telephony system, SDCard R/W access, etc. The greater the access they have, the more they have the chance of snooping. However, most apps are NOT malicious and they need those privileges only to function as per the requirements. For instance, a Camera app will obviously need access to your device camera and the SDCard to store the images. A messaging app will need access to read and send text messages. However, if a Camera app asks access to your Telephony system, you should look at that app suspiciously (it may not necessarily be bad just because it asks for more permissions, though. For example, it could be that the developer has just left that permission on by mistake). Again, as per our analogy it is like your Doctor asking permissions to view your Bank Account details, or your CA asking access to your X-Ray records.

In short, be cautious about what app you install on your device and what permissions you award it.
